title: Before You Sign Up for a Carrier Deal on the iPhone Duo, Know What You’re Getting Into
gist: Wired's shopping guide says Apple rarely discounts the $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo, so carrier deals (up to $1,200 off via 36-month bill credits) are the main route, but they lock the buyer into long plans and a carrier-locked phone. The Duo is back-ordered with shipping into January.

themes.theme: Apple iPhone Duo demand and pricing

insights.claim: Apple almost never discounts its products, especially new ones, and the $2,000-starting iPhone Duo is back-ordered, so no Apple-led sale is expected.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Signals pricing power and strong demand for Apple's first foldable.
insights.quote: Don’t expect Apple to offer a sale on the iPhone Duo. The company almost never discounts its products

insights.claim: Shipping times for the iPhone Duo are stretching into January, indicating supply constraints on Apple's first foldable.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Supply-limited launch supports near-term revenue timing into next quarter.
insights.quote: Shipping times are stretching into January

insights.claim: The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 across Apple, AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, which is very expensive for most buyers.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: A $2,000 foldable tests the ceiling of premium smartphone pricing.

insights.claim: T-Mobile offers $1,200 off the iPhone Duo as 36 monthly bill credits, requiring the Experience Beyond 2.0 plan (about $100 a month) for new customers; it does not apply to full-payment purchases or cheaper plans.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Carriers subsidize premium devices to lock in high-ARPU plan subscribers.
insights.quote: You don’t get $1,200 upfront. Instead, T-Mobile spreads that amount across 36 monthly credits on your bill.

insights.claim: AT&T and Verizon run similar 36-month, roughly $1,200-equivalent incentives; Verizon adds an Apple Watch Series 12 or iPad, and AT&T offers an $800 reward card for switching.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Carrier competition is being fought through device subsidies and bundled hardware.

insights.claim: Carrier deals are effectively contracts: the phone stays locked until the final payment, and the total cost after plan, taxes and fees may equal or exceed current premium plan spending.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: The headline discount is offset by multi-year churn reduction for carriers.
insights.quote: Whichever company’s deal you pursue, you’re entering into what is essentially a contract.

insights.claim: T-Mobile's incentives also extend to the new iPhone 18 Pro and other models, not just the Duo.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Promotional intensity is broad across the iPhone line.

insights.claim: Wired's editors generally recommend buying phones unlocked at full price, but concede carrier deals can make sense for long-term customers who do the math first.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Editorial skepticism of subsidies, which are the main demand lever for expensive phones.
insights.quote: We usually don’t recommend cell phone contracts
